title: Git, GitHub & Team Collaboration
description: Track changes, isolate work, review pull requests, resolve conflicts safely, and coordinate AI assistants without losing work.

lessons.title: Why version control matters
lessons.principle: Version control records project evolution so changes can be compared, discussed, and restored.
lessons.practice: Explain the difference between working tree, staging area, commits, and remote branches.

lessons.title: Protect uncommitted work
lessons.principle: Switching or resetting in a dirty workspace can overwrite edits you intended to keep.
lessons.practice: Inspect git status and save or safely stash relevant changes before a risky operation.

lessons.title: Initialize, clone, and inspect
lessons.principle: A repository has history, branch refs, and a working tree; cloning copies the repository to a local environment.
lessons.practice: Practice git clone, git status, git log, and git diff in a sample project.

lessons.title: Read history for context
lessons.principle: Recent commits explain why a design changed and can expose related bugs or constraints.
lessons.practice: Ask AI to examine the current branch and relevant history before rewriting a subsystem.

lessons.title: Staging and meaningful commits
lessons.principle: A commit should represent one coherent change with an intelligible message.
lessons.practice: Stage only relevant files and inspect the staged diff before committing.

lessons.title: Keep secrets out of Git history
lessons.principle: Deleting a committed secret from the latest file does not necessarily remove it from past commits.
lessons.practice: Use .gitignore, secret scanning, and immediate credential rotation for exposure events.

lessons.title: Branches and isolation
lessons.principle: A branch points to a commit and allows an independent series of changes before integration.
lessons.practice: Create a feature branch from a verified base for the new card deck.

lessons.title: Avoid shared-branch agent collisions
lessons.principle: Multiple agents changing the same branch or files can invalidate one another's assumptions.
lessons.practice: Use isolated branches or worktrees and assign clear file ownership for parallel work.

lessons.title: Pull requests and review
lessons.principle: A pull request provides a bounded diff, rationale, checks, and a discussion before changes join the base branch.
lessons.practice: Write a PR description with purpose, files changed, verification, and known limits.

lessons.title: Review behavior, not only syntax
lessons.principle: A clean diff can still break an API, omit accessibility, or mishandle a failure path.
lessons.practice: Read changed code in context, request tests, and trace affected user journeys.

lessons.title: Merge conflicts
lessons.principle: Conflicts occur when Git cannot automatically reconcile overlapping changes or histories.
lessons.practice: Interpret conflict markers and compare both intended behaviors.

lessons.title: Resolve rather than blindly choose
lessons.principle: Selecting 'ours' or 'theirs' may discard a valid fix from the other side.
lessons.practice: Reconstruct the combined intent, remove markers, run checks, and inspect the final diff.

lessons.title: Rebase and merge tradeoffs
lessons.principle: Merge records integration and rebase rewrites a branch's commits onto a new base.
lessons.practice: Use the collaboration policy of the project instead of rewriting shared history casually.

lessons.title: Keep remote safety in mind
lessons.principle: Force pushing a shared branch can remove colleagues' reachable work.
lessons.practice: Avoid force pushes unless ownership and recovery are understood; prefer safe coordination.

lessons.title: Continuous integration
lessons.principle: Automated checks run against particular commits and configurations when configured.
lessons.practice: Locate workflow files and identify what a green or red check actually verifies.

lessons.title: Associate results with a commit
lessons.principle: A test result from an earlier SHA does not prove that the latest edited head passes.
lessons.practice: Record which final commit and environment a check executed against before claiming readiness.

lessons.title: Reviewing AI-generated diffs
lessons.principle: Generated changes can be large, redundant, or unrelated to the requested scope.
lessons.practice: Use git diff --check and file-by-file review before accepting output.

lessons.title: Preserve provenance
lessons.principle: Automated authorship does not eliminate responsibility for change rationale and behavior.
lessons.practice: Explain what AI changed, what was manually verified, and what remains uncertain in the PR.

lessons.title: Merge and release discipline
lessons.principle: Integration decisions should depend on review, checks, and a known recovery route rather than a green mergeability badge.
lessons.practice: Verify branch freshness and acceptance before merging.

lessons.title: Separate merging from deployment
lessons.principle: A merged commit might still require configuration, data migration, rollout, and monitoring.
lessons.practice: Document release owner, rollback instructions, and post-deployment checks separately from the PR.

git switch -c feat/task-validation
git diff
git add src/task-form.js tests/task-form.test.js

git commit -m "fix: validate task title"

git log --oneline --decorate -5
git diff origin/main...HEAD --stat
git diff --check
# Run the repository's documented checks before requesting review.
